source_text:
32 προσέχετε
ἑαυτοῖς καὶ κρατεῖτε τὰς παραδόσεις ἃς παρελάβετε· μὴ ἐκκλίνητε δεξιὰ μηδὲ
ἀριστερά. 33 καὶ ἐν τούτῳ μνήμην ἔχετε, τέκνα ἀγαπητά, τοῦ μὴ ἀναφέρειν εἰκόνας
ἐπ' ἐκκλησίας μήτε ἐν τοῖς κοιμητηρίοις τῶν ἁγίων· ἀλλ' ἀεὶ διὰ μνήμης ἔχετε τὸν
θεὸν ἐν ταῖς καρδίαις ὑμῶν.
thought_title: Hold the traditions; keep God in memory, not images
orientation: Epiphanius is issuing his testament to the citizens, commanding them to hold fast to the traditions they received and not to bring images into churches or the cemeteries of the saints.
pass_a_gloss: Pay attention to yourselves and hold fast the traditions which you received; do not turn aside to the right nor to the left. And in this matter keep memory, beloved children, of not bringing up images upon churches nor in the cemeteries of the saints; but always through memory keep God in your hearts.

choices.why: The reflexive dative with προσέχω means to attend to or watch over oneself; a direct command.
κρατέω with accusative means to hold firmly or keep; glossary requires 'traditions' for παραδόσεις.

choices.english: do not turn aside to the right nor to the left
choices.why: ἐκκλίνω means to deviate or turn aside; the adverbial accusatives δεξιά and ἀριστερά indicate direction.
rejected: do not swerve right or left
do not lean to the right or the left

choices.why: The articular infinitive with μή expresses the content of the memory they are to keep; ἀναφέρω means to bring up or carry up.

choices.term: διὰ μνήμης ἔχετε τὸν θεὸν ἐν ταῖς καρδίαις ὑμῶν
choices.english: through memory keep God in your hearts
choices.why: διὰ with genitive expresses means; ἔχω with ἐν indicates keeping God present in the heart.
rejected: by remembrance hold God in your hearts
keep God in remembrance in your hearts

pass_b_english: Pay attention to yourselves, and hold fast the traditions you received. Do not turn aside to the right or to the left. And in this, beloved children, keep the memory of not bringing images into churches or into the cemeteries of the saints, but always keep God in your hearts through memory.

problems.why: Four variants of same command blur whether one action or two is meant.
problems.fix: Standardize to 'keep God in memory in your hearts'.

variants.text: keep God in your hearts through memory

problems.why: Same Greek imperative (προσέχετε ἑαυτοῖς) rendered differently.
problems.fix: Use 'Watch yourselves' or 'Pay attention to yourselves' throughout.

problems.why: Minor but unnecessary variation in preposition.
problems.fix: Standardize to 'hold fast to the traditions'.

problems.quote: keep God in memory in your hearts
problems.why: Same concept phrased differently in parallel passages; reader may miss the parallel.
problems.fix: Use identical phrasing across parallel passages.

variants.text: keep God in memory in your hearts
keep God in your hearts through memory

problems.why: Same instruction phrased differently in parallel passages; may confuse a reader comparing them.
problems.fix: Use identical phrasing across parallel passages.

edits.old: And in this, beloved children, keep the memory of not bringing images into churches or into the cemeteries of the saints, but always keep God in your hearts through memory.
edits.new: And in this, beloved children, keep the memory of not bringing images into churches or into the cemeteries of the saints, but always keep God in memory in your hearts.

fixed: The English already uses 'Pay attention to yourselves' consistently in this passage.
The English already uses 'hold fast the traditions' consistently in this passage.
The English already uses 'keep God in memory in your hearts' consistently in this passage.
The English already uses 'keep the memory' consistently in this passage.
